observation.visible_scene: A daytime outdoor shot of a brush-and-log bonfire burning in the middle of a mowed green lawn. A pile of split wood and branches sits on a patch of blackened, charred ground; bright orange flames cover the right/center of the pile, while a thick white-gray smoke column rises from the left edge of the pile and drifts upward and to the left. The background is a line of trees (evergreens and autumn-colored deciduous trees, plus one bare tree) under a clear blue sky. No people or animals are visible.
visible_changes: The orange flames on the pile flicker continuously: their tongues change height, shape and internal brightness from frame to frame, but the flame zone stays in the same location on the pile throughout the excerpt (no ignition onset or burnout is shown).
The smoke plume billows and changes density; wisps detach and swirl at its top, and the upper-left corner of the frame shows smoke appearing and thinning.
Over the clip the smoke column's overall lean shifts from a more vertical rise (early frames) to a stronger leftward tilt (later frames), with the top drifting farther left.
The wood pile, the charred ground patch, the foreground grass and the background tree line remain in essentially fixed positions and shapes; no collapse or rearrangement of the logs is visible.
There is a very slight apparent shift of the whole scene toward the left edge across the frames, suggesting a small slow camera pan/drift, but the background evidence is weak.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the fire was started and whether it is growing or decaying overall (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
The actual wind speed/direction driving the smoke tilt.
Whether anyone is tending the fire (no operator is in frame).
What happens after the last frame (extinguishing, spreading, or continuing).
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain: the small leftward scene shift could be a slow pan, a handheld drift, or just framing noise; the background trees do not give strong parallax.
The exact intensity trend of the flames (steady vs. slightly diminishing) is hard to confirm amid flicker.
Material identity of the burning pile (specific wood types) cannot be determined.
